name: Wallflower
grown_as: The garden wallflower 'Fire King', grown as a biennial: sown in summer, planted out in autumn, flowering the next spring. 'Fire King' has bright orange-red flowers; the wild plant is yellow.
habit: A bushy, upright, rounded plant 30 to 45 cm tall, stems woody at the base and branched, densely leafy, each branch ending in a cluster of flowers.

leaf.outline: Narrowly lance-shaped, 5 to 10 cm long and under 1.5 cm wide
leaf.surface: Flat, with fine flattened hairs that give a slightly dull, greyish sheen

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower, four petals spread flat from a short tube
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded, narrowing to a claw hidden in the sepals
flower.colour: Bright orange-red, often with darker veining; very fragrant
flower.centre: A small greenish centre with the tips of yellow stamens
flower.behind: Four narrow upright sepals pressed close together into a tube below the petals
flower.carried: In a dense rounded cluster at each stem tip that lengthens into a short spike as the lower flowers open, facing up and out

fruit: Long narrow pods 3 to 7 cm, slightly flattened and four-angled, held upright along the lengthening stem, green ripening pale brown and splitting from the bottom. Seeds flat, oval, light brown, about 2 to 3 mm.
seedling: Two small, smooth, round-oval seed leaves on short stalks, then narrow pointed true leaves
winter: Planted out in autumn; through winter a bushy leafy plant of narrow deep green leaves with flower buds forming at the tips.

leaf: narrow lance-shaped leaf with no teeth
bloom: four rounded petals in a cross
sepals pressed together in a tube behind
seedling: two small smooth round-oval seed leaves
first true leaves narrow and pointed
young: a bushy upright plant of many narrow deep green leaves
flower: a bushy plant with dense clusters of orange-red four-petalled flowers at every stem tip
seedhead: long narrow upright pods along the stem tips

look_alikes: Siberian wallflower (Erysimum × marshallii) is bright orange with narrower leaves. Perennial wallflowers such as 'Bowles's Mauve' have grey leaves and mauve flowers. Stocks (Matthiola) have grey felty leaves and pink or purple flowers. Wild wallflower on old walls is yellow.
